question: Change into indirect speech: He said, 'I am tired.'
options: He said that he was tired.
He said that I am tired.
He says that he was tired.
explanation: With a past reporting verb, present 'am' generally backshifts to 'was'.

question: Change into indirect speech: She said to me, 'Do you know him?'
options: She asked me if I knew him.
She told me if I know him.
She asked me that I knew him.
She said to me whether do I know him.
explanation: A yes/no question becomes asked + if/whether + statement order.

question: Change into indirect speech: The teacher said, 'Work hard.'
options: The teacher advised the students to work hard.
The teacher said the students work hard.
The teacher asked that work hard.
explanation: An imperative expressing advice can be reported with 'advised + object + to-infinitive'.

question: Change into indirect speech: Rahul said, 'I have finished my work.'
options: Rahul said that he had finished his work.
Rahul said that he has finished my work.
Rahul says that he had finished his work.
Rahul said that I had finished his work.
explanation: Present perfect generally backshifts to past perfect after a past reporting verb.
